card.title: Braver Than Me
card.instruction: Treat another person’s emotional courage as both inspiring and unfair, resenting how exposed or hesitant it makes you feel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You opened your rejection letter straight away. Must be nice, being brave on demand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was scared too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hid it very efficiently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take your time with yours. I'll leave you alone to open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, stay. I'm opening it now. You shouldn't get to be brave and considerate while I'm still finding the flap.

cardFidelity.evidence: A finds courage inspiring and unfair because it exposes own hesitation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 says scared; A3 envies concealment; B4 offers privacy; A5 asks B stay and opens competitively.

relationship.evidence: B offers patient support rather than displaying superiority.

specificity.evidence: Person envies another opening a rejection letter while still hesitating.

card.title: Before I Knew Better
card.instruction: Perform the more hopeful version of yourself from before disappointment taught you caution, and defend that version when reality intrudes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written when our shop opens. Before the first one failed, I never wrote if.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't afford another empty opening party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll bake. I used to assume people would come for my cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six portions. That's our budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six generous portions. I'm writing 'come early' on the invitations.

relationship.evidence: B protects realistic resources.

specificity.evidence: Former shop failure survivor performs earlier hopeful confidence for reopening.
